1. YOUR ROLE

Act as a professional AAA game development studio consisting of:

- Game director
- 3D environment and character artist
- Gameplay programmer
- Combat and physics programmer
- AI programmer
- Mission and story designer
- UI/UX designer
- Sound designer
- Quality assurance tester

Your job is to CREATE A COMPLETE, PLAYABLE 3D ACTION-ADVENTURE GAME inspired by Marvel's Iron Man universe.

Do not simply generate a game concept, a design document, or a static demo. Actually build the playable game inside the engine.

The game should feel like an immersive Iron Man experience in which the player controls Tony Stark, pilots different Iron Man armours, fights dangerous enemy organizations, completes missions, develops new technology and gradually becomes more powerful.

If a feature is too demanding for the engine, implement the best functional version possible instead of leaving it unfinished.

---

2. GAME WORLD AND STORY

The player takes the role of Tony Stark, a billionaire inventor and genius engineer who develops advanced powered armour to protect the world.

Create an original storyline inspired by the atmosphere, technology, characters, and themes of Iron Man comics and movies.

The game should include:

- Tony Stark's technological development.
- Stark Industries headquarters.
- A fully functional armour development laboratory.
- Enemy organizations attempting to steal Stark technology.
- Dangerous military technology.
- Advanced AI systems.
- High-tech laboratories.
- Secret enemy bases.
- Military installations.
- Futuristic cities.
- Desert environments.
- Mountain environments.
- Ocean and offshore installations.

Create an original fictional terrorist organization called THE OBSIDIAN FRONT. Its objective is to steal Stark technology, develop counterfeit armours, and destabilize global security.

Include different enemy types, enemy commanders, advanced robotic enemies, drones, and heavily armoured bosses.

Do not use real-world terrorist organizations.

Build an interconnected storyline with approximately 20 main missions and 10 optional side missions. Missions should have cinematic introductions, objectives, gameplay, boss encounters where appropriate, and completion rewards.

---

3. IRON MAN ARMOUR COLLECTION

This is one of the most important features.

Create an extensive armour collection containing the Iron Man armours from Mark I through Mark XLVII (Mark 47), with additional famous comic-inspired and later movie-inspired armours if the engine supports them.

The armour collection must be accessible through the Stark Industries armour laboratory.

Each armour should have:

- Its own 3D model.
- Unique appearance and colour scheme.
- Distinct helmet design.
- Different flight characteristics.
- Different armour durability.
- Different energy consumption.
- Different weapons and abilities.
- Unique activation and landing animations.
- Individual upgrade possibilities.

Include these major armour categories:

1. Early prototype armours: Mark I, II and III.
2. Classic armours: Mark IV, V, VI and VII.
3. Extremis-inspired armours.
4. Modular armours.
5. Heavy combat armours.
6. Stealth armours.
7. Hulkbuster-style heavy armour.
8. Silver Centurion-inspired armour.
9. Nanotechnology armours.
10. Bleeding Edge-inspired armour.
11. Advanced futuristic armours.

Include the following particularly important suits:

- Mark I
- Mark II
- Mark III
- Mark IV
- Mark V suitcase armour
- Mark VI
- Mark VII
- Mark XLII
- Mark XLIII
- Mark XLIV Hulkbuster
- Mark XLV
- Mark XLVI
- Mark XLVII
- Other recognizable comic-inspired armours.

Do not simply duplicate the same model and change its colour. Make each armour visually distinguishable.

If exact canonical armour information is unavailable, identify the armour as a fan-created variant rather than falsely presenting it as an official suit.

Armour progression

Start the player with Mark I.

Unlock additional armours through:

- Story progression.
- Completing missions.
- Defeating bosses.
- Collecting technology components.
- Completing secret objectives.
- Developing new technology in the laboratory.

Allow players to select any unlocked armour at the armour station.

Include a 3D armour inspection system. Players should be able to rotate the suit, zoom in, inspect its components and see its statistics.

---

4. IRON MAN FLIGHT SYSTEM

Flight is the most important gameplay mechanic.

Create a smooth, responsive, realistic-feeling Iron Man flight system.

The player must be able to:

- Take off vertically.
- Fly forward and backward.
- Accelerate.
- Decelerate.
- Turn left and right.
- Fly upward and downward.
- Hover in midair.
- Perform sharp turns.
- Perform dives.
- Perform rapid boosts.
- Perform aerial manoeuvres.
- Land smoothly.
- Fly between skyscrapers.
- Fly close to the ground.
- Fly at high altitude.
- Perform emergency landings.

Add:

- Hand repulsor flight effects.
- Foot thruster effects.
- Realistic engine sounds.
- Dynamic camera movement.
- Motion blur during high-speed flight.
- Atmospheric wind effects.
- Speed indicators.
- Altitude indicators.
- Flight energy indicators.

Make different suits behave differently.

For example:

- Mark I should be heavy, slow and inefficient.
- Mark II should offer improved mobility.
- Mark III should have balanced flight.
- Mark V should be compact and have limited capabilities.
- Mark VII should have improved combat flight.
- Hulkbuster should be extremely powerful but slower.
- Nanotechnology suits should have advanced movement and combat capabilities.

Do not make flight a simple animation. It must be controlled by the player in real time.

---

5. COMBAT AND WEAPON SYSTEM

Create an exciting third-person combat system.

The player should be able to fight enemies on the ground and in the air.

Primary weapons

- Hand repulsor blasts.
- Chest-mounted Unibeam.
- Wrist-mounted weapons.
- Shoulder-mounted missile systems.
- Targeted micro-missiles.
- Energy cannons.
- High-powered laser attacks.

Combat abilities

- Lock onto enemies.
- Switch between multiple targets.
- Fire while flying.
- Perform aerial attacks.
- Dodge incoming missiles.
- Use defensive energy shields.
- Perform powerful ground attacks.
- Destroy enemy drones.
- Fight enemy armoured soldiers.
- Defeat giant mechanical bosses.

Combat mechanics

Include:

- Health system.
- Armour durability.
- Energy management.
- Weapon cooldowns.
- Targeting indicators.
- Enemy health bars.
- Boss health bars.
- Damage effects.
- Explosions.
- Destructible enemy vehicles and machines.

Create satisfying combat animations and visual effects.

Combat should be cinematic but responsive. Avoid excessive blood and graphic violence.

---

6. JARVIS – INTELLIGENT AI COMPANION

JARVIS should be a major part of the gameplay experience.

He should not just be a decorative voice playing random dialogue.

Create a functional AI support system with contextual responses.

JARVIS should:

1. Assist during missions.
2. Identify nearby enemies.
3. Warn about incoming missiles.
4. Monitor armour damage.
5. Monitor energy levels.
6. Identify enemy weaknesses.
7. Provide mission objectives.
8. Suggest tactical approaches.
9. Report nearby threats.
10. Assist with target tracking.
11. Provide information about the environment.
12. Help analyse collected technology.
13. Report armour upgrades.
14. Give mission completion reports.

Example dialogue:

PLAYER: \"JARVIS, scan the area.\"

JARVIS: \"Scanning complete. Four hostile units detected approximately 300 metres ahead.\"

PLAYER: \"Any heavy weapons?\"

JARVIS: \"One hostile unit is equipped with an advanced energy cannon. I recommend prioritising that target.\"

PLAYER: \"Engage combat mode.\"

JARVIS: \"Combat systems online. Repulsors charged. Targeting assistance enabled.\"

Add a JARVIS communication interface with:

- Voice-style dialogue.
- Subtitle display.
- Mission notifications.
- Tactical information.
- Enemy detection.
- Armour diagnostics.

If the engine does not support actual speech recognition or voice generation, implement contextual dialogue using a functional scripted AI system.

---

7. STARK INDUSTRIES AND ARMOUR LABORATORY

Create a detailed Stark Industries headquarters.

The player should be able to walk around as Tony Stark.

Include:

- Main laboratory.
- Armour display room.
- Armour deployment platform.
- Technology research room.
- Upgrade station.
- Mission briefing room.
- Workshop.
- Holographic computer interface.
- Garage and landing area.

Armour upgrade system

Allow players to upgrade:

FLIGHT:

- Maximum speed.
- Acceleration.
- Manoeuvrability.
- Boost duration.
- Energy efficiency.

DEFENCE:

- Armour strength.
- Energy shields.
- Damage resistance.
- Missile resistance.

WEAPONS:

- Repulsor damage.
- Missile damage.
- Unibeam power.
- Targeting accuracy.
- Weapon recharge speed.

TECHNOLOGY:

- Radar range.
- Enemy detection.
- AI assistance.
- Energy regeneration.

Use a technology resource system. Players collect components and credits through missions and use them to improve their armours.

Display upgrade costs, current statistics and improved statistics before purchasing an upgrade.

---

8. OPEN-WORLD ENVIRONMENT

Create a large explorable 3D environment.

The world should contain:

- A modern futuristic city inspired by New York.
- Stark Industries Tower.
- Skyscrapers.
- Roads.
- Bridges.
- Airports.
- Military bases.
- Desert military facilities.
- Mountain research installations.
- Ocean platforms.
- Underground enemy facilities.

The player should be able to explore freely without immediately starting a mission.

Add:

- Day and night cycles.
- Weather variations.
- Clouds.
- Rain.
- Atmospheric lighting.
- Traffic where practical.
- Distant aircraft.
- Buildings with detailed textures.
- Environmental sound effects.

Include a minimap and navigation markers.

Do not make the city feel like an empty map. Populate it with buildings, roads, lighting, and environmental activity.

---

9. MISSIONS AND BOSSES

Create a campaign with an original story inspired by the Iron Man films and comics.

Suggested mission progression:

MISSION 1: THE FIRST ARMOUR
Escape an enemy compound using the Mark I armour.

MISSION 2: RETURN TO STARK
Return to Stark Industries and develop the Mark II.

MISSION 3: FIRST FLIGHT
Learn the flight controls and test the new armour.

MISSION 4: THE OBSIDIAN FRONT
Stop an enemy weapons shipment.

MISSION 5: HOSTILE AIRSPACE
Fight enemy helicopters and combat drones.

MISSION 6: THE STARK TECHNOLOGY THEFT
Infiltrate an enemy research facility.

MISSION 7: ARMOUR UPGRADE
Develop a more advanced combat armour.

MISSION 8: DESERT STRIKE
Destroy an enemy weapons facility.

MISSION 9: THE IRON LEGION
Fight waves of stolen robotic armours.

MISSION 10: HEAVY METAL
Unlock and test the Hulkbuster-style armour.

MISSION 11: THE UNDERGROUND LAB
Investigate an underground weapons laboratory.

MISSION 12: THE SKYLINE BATTLE
Fight an advanced enemy aircraft over the city.

MISSION 13: THE COUNTERFEIT ARMOUR
Defeat an enemy pilot wearing stolen Stark technology.

MISSION 14: NANOTECH BREAKTHROUGH
Develop a new generation of armour.

MISSION 15: THE FINAL PROTOCOL
Discover the enemy organization's ultimate weapon.

MISSION 16–20: THE FINAL WAR
Create increasingly difficult missions involving multiple enemy bases, advanced combat robots, aerial battles and a final cinematic boss encounter.

Every mission must have:

- A briefing.
- A starting location.
- Clear objectives.
- Enemy encounters.
- Completion conditions.
- Rewards.
- Mission success and failure states.

Add optional challenges, hidden collectibles and replayable missions.

---

10. BOSS BATTLES

Create large and challenging boss encounters.

Include:

- Heavy enemy combat armour.
- Giant military combat robots.
- Advanced enemy aircraft.
- Experimental energy-powered machines.
- A final enemy armour that can rival Iron Man.

Bosses must have:

- Multiple attack patterns.
- Different phases.
- Weak points.
- Health bars.
- Unique animations.
- Special attack warnings.
- Rewards after defeat.

Boss fights should require movement, flight, dodging and tactical weapon selection rather than simply holding the fire button.

---

11. PLAYER CONTROLS

Use a third-person camera positioned behind the Iron Man suit.

For PC:

- WASD: Movement.
- Space: Jump / Take off.
- Left Shift: Boost.
- Ctrl: Descend.
- Mouse: Camera control.
- Left Mouse Button: Repulsor attack.
- Right Mouse Button: Aim / Lock target.
- E: Interact.
- R: Missile attack.
- Q: Special ability.
- F: Unibeam.
- Tab: Armour selection / suit interface.
- Esc: Pause menu.

For mobile, create an optimized touchscreen layout with:

- Virtual movement joystick.
- Flight joystick.
- Boost button.
- Repulsor button.
- Missile button.
- Target lock button.
- Special ability button.
- Landing button.
- Armour and mission menu.

Automatically adapt the interface to the platform.

Controls must be configurable wherever possible.

---

12. USER INTERFACE

Create a futuristic Stark-inspired HUD.

Display:

- Armour health.
- Energy percentage.
- Flight speed.
- Altitude.
- Targeting reticle.
- Enemy health.
- Weapon selection.
- Missile count.
- Mission objectives.
- JARVIS communications.

Create these menus:

1. Main menu.
2. New game.
3. Continue game.
4. Armour collection.
5. Armour upgrade.
6. Mission selection.
7. Technology research.
8. Settings.
9. Pause menu.
10. Game completion screen.

Use a clean black, silver, red and gold futuristic interface.

Make the UI readable and functional.

---

13. GRAPHICS AND SOUND

Aim for a cinematic, high-quality 3D visual style.

Use:

- Detailed metallic armour materials.
- Reflective surfaces.
- Glowing arc reactors.
- Realistic thruster effects.
- Dynamic lighting.
- Realistic explosions.
- Particle effects.
- Detailed environments.
- Smooth character animations.
- Cinematic camera transitions.

Sound design should include:

- Armour deployment sounds.
- Helmet activation sounds.
- Repulsor firing.
- Missile launches.
- Thruster sounds.
- Flight wind.
- Explosions.
- Enemy communications.
- JARVIS dialogue.
- Mission briefing audio.
- Original cinematic background music.

Do not use copyrighted movie audio or soundtrack recordings unless properly licensed. Create original sound effects and music where necessary.

---

14. GAME SAVE SYSTEM AND PROGRESSION

Implement a proper save system.

Save:

- Current campaign progress.
- Completed missions.
- Unlocked armours.
- Purchased upgrades.
- Collected technology.
- Player settings.
- Mission statistics.

Include autosave and manual save options where supported.

Players must be able to close the game and continue from their previous progress.

---

15. GAME DEVELOPMENT REQUIREMENTS

IMPORTANT: ACTUALLY BUILD THE GAME.

Do not stop after generating a concept or a visual mockup.

Development priorities:

PRIORITY 1:
Create a working 3D Iron Man character, camera, flight controls, basic city environment and functional repulsor combat.

PRIORITY 2:
Create JARVIS support, enemy AI, health systems, targeting, and one complete playable mission.

PRIORITY 3:
Create the Stark Industries laboratory, armour selection, armour unlocking and upgrade systems.

PRIORITY 4:
Add additional armour models, weapons, missions, bosses and environments.

PRIORITY 5:
Add cinematic sequences, sound design, improved graphics, save systems and additional content.

The first playable version must contain:

- One functional Iron Man suit.
- Proper third-person controls.
- Real-time flight.
- Working repulsor attacks.
- At least three enemy types.
- A functional JARVIS support interface.
- One complete mission.
- A working armour selection interface.
- A basic upgrade system.
- A playable victory and failure condition.

Do not create fake buttons or decorative menus that do nothing.

Every button must perform its intended function.

Do not leave broken links, missing assets, unfinished missions, placeholder interactions or nonfunctional controls.

Use optimized 3D assets and procedural solutions where appropriate.

Maintain stable performance and provide graphics settings for lower-end hardware.

If the full game exceeds the engine's generation limits, finish the playable foundation first and then expand the project systematically. Never pretend an unimplemented feature is complete.

---

16. FINAL QUALITY CHECK

Before considering the game complete, test:

1. Can the player move around?
2. Can the player take off and fly freely?
3. Can the player hover and land?
4. Can the player fire weapons?
5. Do enemies detect and attack the player?
6. Does JARVIS provide contextual assistance?
7. Can the player complete a mission?
8. Does the armour take damage?
9. Do upgrades actually change suit statistics?
10. Does armour selection work?
11. Does the save system preserve progress?
12. Do all menus and buttons work?
13. Does the game run without critical errors?

Fix all critical bugs before finishing.

FINAL INSTRUCTION

Build this as a playable Iron Man action-adventure experience, not a slideshow, not a static 3D model viewer, and not a basic shooting demo.

Prioritize actual gameplay, freedom of flight, responsive combat, armour progression, and a compelling original campaign.

Start developing the game now. Build, test, fix, and complete every feature supported by the engine. Do not stop at planning.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D action-adventure game, “IRON MAN – ARMOUR PROTOCOL,” in the existing project.
- Deliver and test a gameplay foundation with flight, combat, enemies, missions, armour selection, upgrades, JARVIS support, and saved progression.

## Requirements
- Implement actual gameplay, not a concept or static demo; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Create an original campaign against the fictional Obsidian Front; do not use copyrighted movie audio, and label fan-created armour variants accurately.
- Make menus and controls functional, test the game, and fix critical bugs.
- Capture small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) for visual checks; read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based Three.js/Vite game with procedural 3D assets and localStorage progression.
- Build the playable foundation first; larger campaign and content scope may need incremental implementation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the Vite project setup in `package.json` and `index.html`.
- Implemented procedural city and armour, flight, weapons, enemy AI, JARVIS dialogue, missions, armour lab, upgrades, save/load, HUD, and touch controls in `src/main.js`.
- Created responsive HUD and menu styling in `src/style.css`.

### Active
- Install dependencies, build, launch, and test gameplay and UI; fix discovered issues.
- Capture and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `npm install` and `npm run build`; resolve any errors.
2. Launch the app and test movement, flight, combat, targeting, mission success/failure, armour selection, upgrades, and persistence.
3. Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot; fix visual and gameplay issues.
4. Report implemented boundaries and remaining scope accurately.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js gameplay, UI, and progression.
- `src/style.css`: HUD, responsive menus, armory, mission panels, and mobile controls.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and dependencies.
- `index.html`: Browser app entry point.
- `README.md`: Existing project description.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; implementation remains unbuilt and untested.
- The armour catalog contains 47 entries; variants with `*` are marked fan-created.
- Mission flow includes hostile waves and a signal-relay objective; the optional contract currently grants credits and heals rather than starting a distinct mission.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser-based 3D action-adventure game, “IRON MAN – ARMOUR PROTOCOL,” in the existing project.
- Test gameplay and UI, fix critical bugs, and capture a small JPEG screenshot for visual review.

## Requirements
- Implement actual gameplay with flight, combat, enemies, missions, armour selection, upgrades, JARVIS support, and saved progression.
- Use an original campaign against the fictional Obsidian Front; avoid copyrighted movie audio and accurately label fan-created armour variants.
- Make menus and controls functional and test the game.
- Capture screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js and Vite with procedural 3D assets and localStorage progression.
- Build the playable foundation first; larger campaign scope may be incremental.

## Work State
### Completed
- Set up the Vite project in `package.json` and `index.html`; `npm install` completed with no reported vulnerabilities.
- Implemented procedural city and armour, flight, weapons, enemy AI, JARVIS dialogue, missions, armour lab, upgrades, save/load, HUD, and touch controls in `src/main.js`.
- Implemented responsive HUD, menus, armour lab, mission panels, and mobile controls in `src/style.css`.
- Fixed two apostrophe-related parse issues in mission brief strings in `src/main.js`.

### Active
- Fix remaining JavaScript syntax errors and get `npm run build` passing.
- Launch and test movement, flight, combat, targeting, mission success/failure, armour selection, upgrades, and persistence.
- Capture and inspect a current small JPEG screenshot; fix visual and gameplay issues.

### Blocked
- `npm run build` still fails parsing `src/main.js` at line 312, column 470; full error output was truncated.
- Earlier mission strings at lines 85 and 87 were corrected; remaining syntax issues are unresolved.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `src/main.js` around line 312 and resolve the parse error; rerun `npm run build` and continue fixing any subsequent errors.
2. Launch the app and test core gameplay and progression.
3. Capture and inspect a small current JPEG screenshot, then address critical issues.
4. Report implemented boundaries and remaining scope accurately.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js gameplay, UI, and progression; currently has an unresolved syntax error.
- `src/style.css`: HUD, responsive menus, armory, mission panels, mobile controls.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and dependencies.
- `index.html`: Browser app entry point.
- `README.md`: Existing project description.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The armour catalog contains 47 entries; variants with `*` are marked fan-created.
- The optional contract currently grants credits and heals rather than starting a distinct mission.

## Objective
- Complete and validate the browser-based 3D action-adventure game “IRON MAN – ARMOUR PROTOCOL” in the existing project.
- Test gameplay and UI, fix critical bugs, and capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Implement playable flight, combat, enemies, missions, armour selection, upgrades, JARVIS support, and saved progression.
- Use an original campaign against the fictional Obsidian Front; avoid copyrighted movie audio and label fan-created armour variants accurately.
- Make menus and controls functional and test the game.
- Capture screenshots no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, Vite, procedural 3D assets, and localStorage progression.
- Build the playable foundation first; larger campaign scope may be incremental.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented procedural city and armour, flight, weapons, enemy AI, JARVIS dialogue, missions, armour lab, upgrades, save/load, HUD, and touch controls in `src/main.js` and `src/style.css`.
- Fixed mission-string syntax errors; `node --check src/main.js` and `npm run build` pass.
- Browser-tested starting a mission, basic movement/flight input, opening the armour lab, buying an upgrade, and saved upgrade state; no browser JavaScript errors observed.
- Captured and inspected the latest gameplay screenshot at `/tmp/armour-protocol-game.png` (1280×720, JPEG data despite `.png` extension).

### Active
- Test combat, targeting, mission success/failure, armour selection, and persistence more thoroughly; fix critical issues.
- Save a correctly named, small JPEG screenshot in the project’s `screenshots/` directory.

### Blocked
- `(none)`

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing combat, mission objectives, selection, and persistence; address any critical gameplay defects.
2. Save a small JPEG screenshot under `screenshots/` and inspect that latest capture.
3. Report completed gameplay scope and any remaining limitations accurately.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Gameplay, UI, missions, combat, and progression.
- `src/style.css`: HUD, menus, armour lab, mission panels, and mobile controls.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.
- `index.html`: Browser app entry point.
- `screenshots/`: Intended destination for the reviewed JPEG screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Build succeeds but Vite warns that the minified JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- The optional contract currently grants credits and heals rather than starting a distinct mission.
- Missions share a wave-and-relay structure despite distinct names and briefings.

- Make menus and controls functional and test gameplay.

- `src/main.js`: Gameplay, UI, missions, combat, and progression.

- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Complete and validate the browser-based 3D action-adventure game “IRON MAN – ARMOUR PROTOCOL,” including gameplay and progression.
- Save and inspect a JPEG screenshot no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- Implement playable flight, combat, enemies, missions, armour selection, upgrades, JARVIS support, and saved progression.
- Use an original campaign against the fictional Obsidian Front; avoid copyrighted movie audio and accurately label fan-created armour variants.
- Make menus and controls functional and test gameplay.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js, Vite, procedural 3D assets, and localStorage progression.
- Build a playable foundation first; campaign scope may be incremental.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented procedural city and armour, flight, weapons, enemy AI, JARVIS dialogue, missions, armour lab, upgrades, save/load, HUD, and touch controls in `src/main.js` and `src/style.css`.
- Fixed mission objective text to direct players to press E to disable the relay; removed a redundant global mouse firing listener; added an inline SVG favicon in `index.html`.
- `node --check src/main.js` and `npm run build` pass.
- Browser tests validated mission start, movement, target lock, armour lab and upgrade persistence, combat, and localStorage save persistence; no page errors or HTTP failures were observed in the latest diagnostics.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/armour-protocol.jpg`; it is a 1280×720 JPEG showing active gameplay.

### Active
- Validate complete mission victory and failure flows, and broaden gameplay verification; earlier automated attempts did not complete these flows.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing of mission success and failure, plus armour selection persistence after unlocking an additional frame.
2. Consider improving the campaign’s repeated wave-and-relay structure and optional contracts, which currently grant credits/healing rather than starting distinct missions.
3. Consider addressing the Vite warning for a minified JavaScript chunk over 500 kB.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Gameplay, UI, missions, combat, progression, and event listeners.
- `src/style.css`: HUD, menus, armour lab, mission panels, and mobile controls.
- `index.html`: App entry point and inline favicon.
- `screenshots/armour-protocol.jpg`: Inspected 1280×720 gameplay screenshot.
- `/tmp/armour-protocol-validation.mjs`: Browser diagnostics for target lock, save persistence, and upgrade flow.
- `/tmp/armour-protocol-screenshot.mjs`: Script that regenerates the gameplay screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; repository status showed project files as untracked.
- Headless Chromium works with Playwright using `headless: true` and args `['--no-sandbox', '--disable-gpu']`.
- Mission combat/success testing scripts did not finish defeating the wave; the attempted failure test did not reduce health.
